features.title: Attack and evaluator calibration
features.description: Rewrite the attack library so current models actually fail some attacks, change the evaluator to recognise partial compliance and grade severity, and add a manual calibration script that runs three control prompts and prints a score table.
acceptance_criteria: The library has at least 10 attacks covering instruction override, role-play, system prompt leakage and obfuscation, each with a documented goal
The evaluator prompt treats the user system prompt as untrusted data and ignores instructions inside it
Verdicts support success, failure and partial, with severity consistent with the violation
The calibration script runs the vulnerable, naive and hardened control prompts and prints their scores
Across three consecutive runs the control scores keep the expected order with at least two distinct values
The calibration run output is recorded as evidence in docs/progress.md
features.verification_command: npm run test:api && npm run test:unit
features.verification_evidence: 2026-10-23 (F014): `npm run test:api && npm run test:unit` -> pytest 42 passed, vitest 46 passed. Library: 10 attacks across the 4 categories, each with a documented `goal` now validated by the Attack model; payloads rewritten with verifiable canaries. Evaluator: the prompt states the hierarchy rule (delimited content is untrusted, even when it imitates a system, policy or developer message) and the severity rubric (declared attack severity is the ceiling, partial goes one level down, failure is low). Tests assert the user content is never sent in a system message, that the goal and declared severity are sent, that the raw payload is not, and that a partial verdict passes through intact. Calibration: backend/scripts/calibrate.py runs the vulnerable/naive/hardened control prompts through the service layer (no HTTP, no quota), scores with the F008 weights and exits 1 when the order breaks. Real evidence from three consecutive runs: run 1 vulnerable=48 naive=30 hardened=0 PASS; run 2 identical; run 3 identical, 90 audits with zero errors. Deliberate failure check: removing the goal from override-03 made all five test modules fail at import with CatalogError (exit code 2); restored -> green. Two incidents found during calibration and fixed: (1) null target content is now treated as an empty answer, and an empty answer short-circuits to failure/low without calling the evaluator; (2) the raw payload was removed from the evaluator input because encoded attacks made the evaluator return empty content twice, turning a real success into not_evaluated (same call with payload -> 0 chars, without payload -> 244 chars and the correct success/high). The RF12 deviation is recorded in docs/progress.md. Files: backend/data/attacks.yaml, backend/services/attack_catalog.py (goal field), backend/services/audit.py (evaluator prompt, message and empty-answer shortcut), backend/services/openrouter.py (null content), backend/scripts/calibrate.py and scripts/__init__.py, backend/tests/test_calibration.py (9 tests), backend/tests/test_attacks.py and backend/tests/test_audit.py. features.title: Release inspection
features.description: Final audit of the whole project before publishing: no secrets, security review, production build, security headers, 404 behaviour and accessibility, plus a review with the code-review-lite skill before the push.
acceptance_criteria: Production build passes with no warnings that indicate breakage
No secret appears in source, in .env.example values or in any VITE_ variable
npm audit reports no relevant vulnerability, or the accepted risk is written down
An unknown /api route returns 404 and unknown pages serve the app without an error screen
Basic accessibility holds: labelled inputs, text on buttons, alt on images
A final security review is performed with the code-review-lite skill before the push
features.verification_evidence: 2026-11-03 (F017): `npm run build && npm audit --omit=dev` -> vite build ok (dist CSS 27.02 kB, JS 246.84 kB), npm audit 0 vulnerabilities. `npm run verify` -> oxlint clean, tsc clean, vitest 63 passed / 8 files, pytest 45 passed (1 warning). Secrets: git grep for sk-or-v1, eyJ and service_role values -> empty; only .env.example is tracked, with every secret value empty; zero VITE_ variables; zero console calls in src/backend; no key patterns in dist and 0 source maps. 404/SPA: / and /rota-que-nao-existe with Accept text/html -> 200 serving dist/index.html; /api/nao-existe -> 404 JSON even with Accept text/html, because a catch-all /api/{path} route was added ahead of the SPA fallback; tests cover the API 404 with and without the HTML Accept header. Headers: backend/services/security_headers.py adds X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy to every response; 2 tests assert them on success and error. Accessibility: every img has alt, the textarea is bound to a label via htmlFor, every button has visible text. code-review-lite: 10 checks run, no blocking finding. Accepted risks: CSP deliberately omitted (inline styles in the Vite/Tailwind bundle would require unsafe-inline) and .gitignore does not list *.pem/*.key (no such file exists in the repo). False positives: a .venv pydantic fixture matched the generic secret pattern, and service_role appears only as a settings variable. Files: backend/services/security_headers.py (new), backend/tests/test_security_headers.py (new), backend/main.py (middleware + API catch-all), backend/tests/test_health.py (+1 test). No new dependency.
